top.line: News should sell the evidence, not the article
top.para: Advertising and subscriptions both fail the reader, and falling search traffic and consumer law arriving in January 2027 are dismantling them. The proposal is to treat the story as a fractal semantic graph, with the article as one projection, and sell five things from it in pence to readers, firms and agents, paying whoever made the facts.

s0.line: Sell five projections of one evidenced story graph
s0.para: The whole argument in ten points: both models fail readers and are being dismantled, the goal is a loop that funds investigative work, and the article is one projection of a fractal graph. Five things can be sold, revenue would split 60/25/10/5 towards the researcher, and parts already run, though the billing does not.

s1.line: Advertising sells the reader; subscriptions charge rent on disuse
s1.para: Under advertising the reader is inventory and content is bait; under subscriptions the reader pays 100% for the 10% they use, as in one household paying roughly £50 a month. Neither funds reliability, so investigative work is cut first. Reuters Institute 2026 data puts trust in news at 37% and news avoidance at 42%.

s2.line: The goal is a model that rewards investigative journalism
s2.para: Not a better paywall or a cheaper subscription, but a loop: evidenced reporting drives on-demand use by readers, firms and agents, that use produces revenue independent of search traffic and subscriber inertia, and the revenue funds more reporting. A proposal that does not reward the reporting is not part of the model, however well it monetises.

s3.line: Search traffic and subscription inertia are both being removed
s3.para: Organic Google traffic to publishers fell 33% globally in the year to November 2025, and Cloudflare now tolls AI crawlers with HTTP 402. Only 17% pay for online news, and UK subscription rules, brought forward to 1 January 2027, remove the inertia subscriptions depend on. The industry still answers with more subscriptions and personalisation.

s4.line: Micropayment critiques assume a reader; today's buyers differ
s4.para: James Ball's 2020 case and Blendle's record, 150,000 payers among more than a million users, show readers will not weigh twenty pence per article. But the buyers have changed: the reader wants one item, the firm wants a licence to transform and forward it, and the agent pays per query to learn whether it is true.

s5.line: The story is a graph; articles are projections
s5.para: A story is claims, evidence, sources, raw materials and drafts; the article is one walk through it, and the industry sells that cheapest projection while the graph decays. The dataset is worth more than the words, which any model can regenerate. I have argued this since February 2025, before the evidence arrived to confirm it.

s6.line: Meaning lives in edges, and every node opens further
s6.para: In a Fractal Semantic Graph every edge is a verb with a named inverse, such as evidenced_by or contradicts, which is how reporters already connect facts. Zooming into any node opens its own world. This gives provenance down to the byte, corrections that propagate, projections sized to the question, and credit for doors that turned out empty.

s7.line: Evidence is hashed bytes, provenance the path, trust earned
s7.para: Evidence is frozen, SHA-256 hashed bytes rather than links. Provenance is the path of named edges from a claim down to that evidence, a checkable statement of what it rests on rather than of truth. Trust is earned when walked provenance keeps holding. Each step can be sold, and the article alone contains none of them.

s8.line: A vault holds the whole story as one unit
s8.para: An encrypted, versioned vault holds the text, evidence, story graph, sources, translations and prompts. Sources are frozen and hashed, claims are superseded rather than deleted, anonymous sources are flagged for automatic redaction, and credibility is computed from consistency. A worked example cost £8.40 and six hours twenty-three minutes of compute, with zero human hours.

s9.line: One graph yields five products, with the article free
s9.para: The public article stays free and findable as the door. The licensed article sells in pence to readers and as a licence to transform for firms. The evidence vault serves analysts and lawyers, customised projections cut the graph per role or language, and the verification API sells warranted, on-record confirmation per query.

s10.line: Payments should flow mostly to whoever made the fact
s10.para: The proposed split is 60% to the original researcher, 25% to the data organisation, 10% to the journalist and 5% to the outlet, which today captures nearly everything. Paying sources requires a graph that names them. Rails such as x402 now make payments in pence viable, though nothing on sgit.ai is wired to them yet.

s11.line: The substrate already runs in public, cheaply
s11.para: Working pieces include the hash-verified Regulation Graph, VoiceDebrief, a penetration test report with eight audience views, and the Portuguese newsroom with 92 frozen sources, 312 nodes and 942 edges behind an editor-gated pipeline. The whole estate of thirty-one vaults is 2,662 files and 295 MB, so even one journalist could run it.

s12.line: Eight steps a publisher could start this quarter
s12.para: Store stories as graphs from day one and freeze and hash every source. Keep the public article free and findable, sell licensed articles in pence, and adopt the five subscription clauses before January. License the evidence vault to B2B buyers, put corrections in the graph, and publish the cost per story.

s13.line: The graph, not the words, is what buyers miss
s13.para: The industry sells the output whose marginal cost has gone to zero and discards the asset that has not. The evidence, trail, on-record confirmation and tailored view, paid in pence to those who made the facts, is the product. Take away the words and few notice; take away the graph and lawyers, analysts and agents do.
